text:
**Short answer: LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** NMC only makes sense if weight matters most or you'll use the unit rarely.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated 3,000-4,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-800 for NMC. That's about 8-11 years of daily use versus 1.5-2 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). One source lists NMC at 1,000-2,000 cycles ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)), so ratings vary.
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed more mildly. They reached lower peak temperatures and produced smoke rather than flames ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). It isn't fireproof, though. One study found LFP reached thermal runaway sooner in an overcharge test, and DOE notes LFP systems have had incidents too ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Price:** The cost gap has largely closed. One retailer's data shows median prices of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Market:** Nearly all current stations are LFP. NMC is mostly older or compact models.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Cell-level energy density** is higher. But in finished stations the weight gap is small, about 10-16% per pound in two datasets. The inverter and case weigh the same either way. Some LFP stations are even lighter per Wh than some NMC ones.

**Cold weather is not a clear differentiator.** Some sites say LFP is better in the cold, but others found that both chemistries typically refuse to charge below 32°F. Check the specific model's charging temperature range.

**Rule of thumb**
- **Daily or near-daily use (van, off-grid, UPS):** LiFePO4.
- **A few outages a year:** Either works, since calendar aging will matter more than cycles.
- **Weight-critical:** Compare specific models by actual weight.
- **Always check the spec sheet** for the chemistry and the cycle rating's end point (80% vs 70%).
